---
title: "SPEC-4.2.0-v001"
subtitle: "Preview panel redesign, domain browsing, move undo, selection memory"
---

## Overview

A batch of UX changes driven by hands-on feedback: smarter tab selection,
a redesigned preview panel, a move-to-any-window flow with multi-level
undo/redo, a domain browser, relabeled sidebar actions that act on the
*displayed* tabs, and two bug fixes.

## 1. Per-window selection memory

Clicking a window in the sidebar (or drilling into a window card) now
selects the tab that was **last selected in that window**; if none was
ever selected — or that tab is gone — the window's **first tab** is
selected. The preview panel follows the selection, so it no longer keeps
showing a tab from the previous window.

- The memory is a session-only `windowId → tabId` map
  (`lastSelectedByWindowRef`); it is deliberately **not persisted**
  because Chrome tab ids are not stable across browser restarts.

## 2. Smart selection when closing the previewed tab

Closing the currently previewed tab no longer blanks the preview panel.
The tab that visually takes the closed tab's place in the current list is
selected (the next one in display order; when the last row is closed, the
new last row). The preview only goes empty when the list itself is empty.

## 3. Preview panel redesign

- The sibling-tab **pill strip is gone** (it consumed too much space and
  was confusing with many same-site tabs). It is replaced by a one-row
  **tab navigator**: ◀ ▶ arrows step through the window's tabs (wrapping),
  and a **"Tab N of M" dropdown** opens a scrollable list of every tab in
  the window — row number, favicon, and full title, with the current tab
  highlighted.
- The `WINDOW` boilerplate badge is replaced by plain text
  **"Current Window:"**; the highlight moved onto the actual window name
  (real data), not the label.
- A browser-style **address bar** now shows the **full URL** of the
  previewed tab, truncated with the full value on hover, plus a
  **copy button** (shows a ✓ for a moment after copying).

## 4. Check All ↔ Uncheck All

The toolbar "Check All (N)" button now stays visible while tabs are
checked and flips to **"Uncheck All (N)"** once every displayed tab is
checked. The ✕ button still clears any selection (including checks that
span other views).

## 5. Moving tabs: any window, no focus steal, multi-level undo

- The "Move N" toolbar button is now **"Move N ▾"** — a dropdown offering
  **New Window** plus **every existing window** (sorted by name, with tab
  counts). Windows that already contain all the checked tabs are disabled.
- **TabMaster stays the active window** after every move:
  `tabService.moveTabs` no longer focuses the target window, and
  `createWindowWithTabs` creates the window unfocused and then explicitly
  refocuses the TabMaster window.
- **Multi-level undo/redo for tab moves**: every move (toolbar menu, tab
  context menu, window context menu "Move Checked Tabs Here", group
  context menu) records where each tab came from (window + position).
  Undo/Redo arrow buttons appear in the toolbar once a move has happened.
  - Undo moves tabs back to their original window at their original index
    (ascending-index order so positions restore correctly). Tabs closed
    since the move — or whose original window is gone — are skipped, with
    a notification stating how many could not be restored.
  - Redo re-applies the move; "New Window" redo creates a fresh window.
  - The stacks are session-only and unlimited depth.

## 6. Bug fix: stuck indexing badge/spinner

The page-text indexing counter next to the search-scope pill froze (e.g.
at "9") with a forever-spinning icon if the scope changed or the query cleared
mid-indexing: the effect cleanup stopped the countdown without resetting
the counter. The cleanup now resets `indexingRemaining` to 0.

## 7. Domain browsing

- The sidebar header now reads
  **"N Windows • N Tabs • N Domains ▾ • vX.Y.Z"**. The domain count is a
  button (with a chevron as the affordance hint) that opens a
  **searchable dropdown** listing every distinct domain with its tab
  count.
- Picking a domain enters a new **`ViewMode.BY_DOMAIN`** view: a flat
  list of just that domain's tabs, titled "Domain: <name>" with an ✕ to
  exit back to All Tabs. In card view the **Window** metadata field is
  forced visible there (the window a tab lives in is part of the point);
  the detail view already has a Window column.
- Pages without a real URL (chrome://, local files) group under `local`.

## 8. Sidebar relabels + displayed-tabs scope

- **"Organize by Website" → "Categorize by Website"**,
  **"Organize with AI" → "Categorize with AI"** (short labels, no
  tooltips, per user preference).
- **"All Tabs" → "Display tabs from all windows"**, moved from Views into
  the **Window Controls** section (it is a window-filter reset, not a
  categorization). Keyboard focus order follows the new visual order.
- **Behavior change**: both Categorize actions now operate on the
  **currently displayed tabs** (respecting the active window/domain
  filter and search), not on every open tab:
  - *Categorize by Website* snapshots the displayed tab ids
    (`categorizeScopeIds`) and groups only those.
  - *Categorize with AI* sends only the displayed tabs to Gemini (its
    cached-result signature is computed over the same set).
  - Both clear sidebar window selections on entry (the grouped views
    don't render while sidebar multi-select is active).

## 9. Documentation & guide

- The interactive tour gained a **"Browse by Domain"** step and its
  copy was updated for the renamed buttons, the new preview panel, the
  Move ▾ menu, and selection memory.
- `README.md` Features/User Guide sections rewritten to match 4.2.0.
- `UserGuideModal` now **renders the guide as formatted UI** (headings,
  lists, code, links, quotes — via a small dependency-free markdown
  renderer) instead of dumping raw markdown text.

## Version

`package.json` / `manifest.json` bumped **4.1.1 → 4.2.0**.
